subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should OpenClaw enforce a default Docker sandbox PID cap when `sandbox.docker.pidsLimit` is omitted, and what opt-out/upgrade contract should ship with it?
rationale: This is a security hardening improvement, but it changes the runtime behavior of existing configs and could affect legitimate high-process sandbox workloads after recreation.

options.title: Approve default cap with alignment
options.body: Require the PR or replacement to add maintainer-approved default value semantics, opt-out behavior, schema/type/docs/tests, and live Docker proof before merge.

options.title: Keep PID cap opt-in
options.body: Leave omitted `pidsLimit` as Docker default/unlimited and close or pause this PR unless a separate approved strict default is designed.

options.title: Choose a different cap or migration
options.body: Use this PR as the starting point but change the value or add a doctor/setup path before existing users see the new default.

recommendation.title: Approve default cap with alignment
recommendation.body: Require the PR or replacement to add maintainer-approved default value semantics, opt-out behavior, schema/type/docs/tests, and live Docker proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sandbox hardening history and ownership-adjacent CODEOWNERS context make this the best available routing candidate for the security/default decision.
